To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of GABAergic activity in embryonic retinal cell aggregates in culture is modulated by GABA, a major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system.

the addition of GABA (a neurotransmitter) to the culture medium of embryonic avine retina cells in culture prevents the expression of glutamate decarobxylase activity, an enzyme that converts glutamic acid (an excitatory neurotransmitter) to GABA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation by GABA of GAD activity in embryonic retina-cell cultures.
the regulation of GAD expression by γ-aminobutyrate (GABA).
the regulation of GAD expression in embryonic retinal cells in culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABA-mediated reduction in GAD activity and immunoreactivity is the result of an action at the level of the neuron and not at the level of enzyme biosynthesis.
the GABA-mediated decrease in GAD activity is a consequence of a direct effect of GABA on the GABAergic neurons of the retina-cell aggregate cultures.
the presence of GABA in the culture medium inhibits the expression of GABAA receptors and the synthesis of GAD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GABA, acting through its receptor, inhibits GAD expression in embryonic retina cells in culture.
GABA acts as an inhibitor of GAD in retinal neurons.
the GAD activity of embryonic retinal cells in culture is regulated by γ-aminobutyrate (GABA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
GABA can regulate the expression of GABAergic neurotransmitters.

GABA is a potent inhibitor of GAD activity and GAD immunoreactivty in embryonic retina cell aggregates in culture, and that this action of GABA may play a role in the differentiation of the embryonic retina.
GABA is able to regulate GAD expression in cultured embryonic retina neurons.
